hold_text: The diff edits scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py, which is in LANDING_MACHINERY, so R12 bars self-landing by construction -- the change and its own approval would be the same act, and a mistake in it disarms the very check that would have caught the mistake. THIS IS NOT WAITING ON AN APPROVAL AND MUST NOT BE RE-SOUGHT: it needs a human merge click. The edit to that guard is FOUR LINES, identical to the other 23 -- a lazy import of scripts/ci/_dirty_tree.py and one warn() call after parse_args -- and it changes no verdict, no exit code and no rule. It is in the diff because check_pr_landing.py is itself one of the guards a session types after a red check, and it is one of the FOUR guards that produced the instances this row was filed on, so omitting it would leave out the guard that actually bit.
why: Tier-1 TOOLING: one new scripts/ci/ module (_dirty_tree.py), one new test file, 24 guards gaining four lines each, run_guards.py gaining a child-env suppression, and one AMENDED backlog row. No src/, no config/, no deploy/. WHAT IT IMPLEMENTS: BL-20260917-THE-DIRTY-TREE-NOTICE-LIVES-ONLY-IN-RUN-GUARDS-SO-ALL-18-DIRECTLY-INVOCABLE-DIFF-SCOPED-GUARDS-STILL-GRADE-THE-WRONG-TREE-SILENTLY, filed on four instances in one day, all by this author. Every --base guard grades a COMMIT RANGE; the 2026-09-13 remedy went into run_guards.py alone, and a session chasing one failure types the single guard the failure named rather than the 15-minute orchestrator. [!] THE ROW'S OWN POPULATION FIGURE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED IN IT. Re-measured by DERIVING the set: 26 scripts accept --base, 24 of which run_guards.py invokes -- that is the population that matters, because a script run_guards never runs is not one a session types after a red check. And '18 of 18 carry no notice' was false: handoff_check.py matches a keyword scan, for a DIFFERENT concern (manager state not pushed to origin). Honest form: 0 of 24 carry THIS notice, 1 of 24 mentions the word for an unrelated reason. The test therefore DERIVES the population at collection time instead of freezing a list -- the frozen count was wrong by six inside a day. DESIGN: three never-collapsed states (clean SILENT, dirty, could_not_look which is NOT silence), stderr only so it cannot contaminate a guard's parsed stdout, NO change to any exit code, untracked files counted as dirty deliberately, and an opt-IN suppressor so an unset variable leaves the notice ON and a typo cannot silence it. VERIFIED LIVE ON BOTH ARMS, not from the unit tests: dirty tree -> 24 of 24 print; clean tree -> 0 of 24. [!] TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN CHANGE, BOTH FOUND BY MEASURING IT. (1) The fix introduced the alarm it prevents: run_guards spawns each guard as a subprocess, so the notice printed once per sub-invocation -- MEASURED at 4 copies from a SINGLE selected guard, since a guard's self-test and its real run are separate processes. run_guards now spawns children with DIRTY_TREE_NOTICE=0; verified 0 per-guard notices inside the orchestrator and 1 when the same guard is typed directly. (2) The comment inserted into all 24 files CITED THE ROW BY A TRUNCATED ID; artifact-validity-guard refused it and named every file. That is the FOURTH truncated id from this author in one day, caught ONLY because the guard was run on COMMITTED STATE -- the discipline this notice exists to prompt. CONTROLS: 63 tests, SEVEN defects planted, SEVEN caught, including a PARTIAL fix (one guard losing the call), which is the plant that matters when the change is 24 mechanical edits. The runner asserts each patch actually changed the file before trusting its result, after two plants silently failed to apply earlier today and printed a green line indistinguishable from an absorbed plant. FULL GUARD SET on committed state: PASS 109 · FAIL 1 · COULD-NOT-RUN 0 · SKIP 0, the one failure being pr-landing-guard, which the arming push is the second half of. [!] CI MAY SHOW register-id-guard RED THROUGH NO FAULT OF THIS PR: main currently carries a duplicate register id (1607 rows / 1606 unique), which reds every backlog-touching PR in the repo. PR #12399 repairs it. Register integrity: amended through update_row, 1 insertion / 1 deletion, --check-live byte-for-byte on all four registers. ruff clean.
